clue.text: Wrongly taken lives right doctor conceals

indicators.note: whatever conceals something wraps around it, so the doctor's letters go outside

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine
'is' as in 'lives' or exists
right in the sense of fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A doctor is hiding someone's life savings that were taken by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lives reads as a plural noun, but it is the verb 'exists'; right is the adjective meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Misappropriated funds are ones dishonestly or wrongly taken for one's own use.

clue.text: Piece risks accommodating popular feature on English language

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room inside, so the following words go within

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
dares as a verb, ventures or risks
in means fashionable or popular
a facial feature
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A chess piece takes risks to grab a popular spot on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on English' puts the abbreviation for English at the bottom, after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin Chinese is the most widely spoken variety of Chinese, the official tongue of China.

clue.text: Band splits up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: splits as a verb: separates, parts

explanation.surface: A pop group breaks up and goes separate ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a band of leather or fabric used to fasten or hold something.

clue.text: Plain look that is introduced by priest

parts.note: Pr is an abbreviation for priest
an air is a look or appearance
i.e., Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A priest presents an unadorned appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced by priest' puts PR at the front of AIR + IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, a type of plain in North America.

clue.text: Let guards train in uniform

indicators.note: something that guards another surrounds it protectively, so it goes on the outside

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: Soldiers are allowed to guard the train while dressed in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: Train is a verb, to point a weapon, not a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for clothing, which a uniform is.

clue.text: Falsely claim cardinal died after prior

indicators.note: after puts the words before it second, so the cardinal and died follow prior

parts.note: pre- means before or prior
a cardinal number
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone lies that a cardinal died after the prior of a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal and prior look like churchmen; one is a number and the other means before.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make a false claim or put on a show of something untrue.

clue.text: Second of this month

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a moment, a very short time

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a date, the second of the month; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment of time, and in dated commercial letters 'inst.' or instant refers to the current month.

clue.text: End of gnat's body eaten by another insect

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so these letters go within

parts.note: the first part of the insect that eats wood

indicators.note: the body of a word is its middle, without the extremities

parts.note: the middle letters of gnat
the rest of the same insect

explanation.surface: A gnat comes to a sticky end, devoured by a bigger insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of gnat' tempts you to take a final letter T, but End alone is the definition and 'of' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end or finish it.

clue.text: In English, it's not a clear piece of writing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the article in English that is not the indefinite one, namely 'the'
second meaning: clear is definite, and a piece of writing is an article

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it read as a complaint about muddled English prose; the split falls after 'a', which is itself the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The' is the definite article in English grammar, the counterpart of 'a', and a definite article could also be an unambiguous essay.

clue.text: Make regular sailor upset with men

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Restoring order when a sailor is angry with the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring something back to a standard, regular state.

clue.text: Foot gets inflamed when twisted

indicators.note: twisted round means turned to face the other way, so read backwards

parts.note: fires up, catches alight

explanation.surface: A foot becomes swollen and painful after being twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot sounds medical here, but it is the typographic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke projecting at the foot or top of a letter in some typefaces.

clue.text: Falsely accuse those introducing asylum seekers essentially

indicators.note: the ones that introduce the words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of each word
per se, Latin for intrinsically or essentially

explanation.surface: Smearing people who bring asylum seekers into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to spread damaging, false charges about someone, to slander them.

clue.text: Means of avoiding store returning charged item

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so read backwards

parts.note: to store up is to save
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: Taking a charged item back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Store looks like a shop, but it is a verb meaning save.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is a dodge, a way of getting out of or avoiding something.

clue.text: Reporter's not at all religious

definitions.note: a noun: a religious is a member of a religious order

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so what follows is how the word is heard

parts.note: none means not at all

explanation.surface: A journalist confesses to having no faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A religious' as a noun means a monk or nun.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a woman in a religious order, so is a religious in the noun sense.

clue.text: Loan what is left by Independent politician

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Member of Parliament
the rest is the remainder

explanation.surface: A loan left behind by an Independent MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts the remainder next to the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is an advance of money, a loan made for a specific purpose, often by the state.

clue.text: Relevant point in a part of the Bible

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other words that follow

parts.note: a as in 'ten pounds a day', meaning per
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler
New Testament

explanation.surface: A pertinent point found in a Bible passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' meaning per, as in 'twice a day', is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinent means directly applicable or to the point, which is what relevant means.

clue.text: Drunkard shouts out at regular intervals

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A drunk keeps shouting every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: A sot is a habitual heavy drinker, an old word for a drunkard.

clue.text: Reduce the value of French region

parts.note: de, French for of
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Looks like a question about property prices in part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Reduce the value', with 'of' joining it to the wordplay; 'detract from' means diminish.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract is to take away from the worth or merit of something.

clue.text: Period drama recreates revolutionary circles

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the letters run backwards
the words circle the target, holding it inside them

parts.note: spanning the end of drama and start of recreates

explanation.surface: A costume drama re-creates the circles of revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period drama' looks like one phrase, but Period alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history marked by some distinctive feature.

clue.text: Stays determined to stop island crushing resistance

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so these letters are inserted inside
crushing something means pressing it between, so it holds the next item inside

parts.note: Kos or Cos, a Greek island
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
set on, determined

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to halt an island's suppression of a resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: COS crushes R to make CORS, and SET then plugs it: COR(SET)S. Stays is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are corsets, stiffened underclothes, from the strips of bone that support them.

clue.text: Vocal cover-up and mounting interference stopped by individual's case

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means climbing upward, read from the bottom
something stopped by a plug has it lodged inside

parts.note: noise is interference on a signal

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of individual

explanation.surface: A singer covers up mistakes while rising background noise is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first, then the whole string climbs; 'Vocal cover-up' is a playful description of a sound being swallowed in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision is the dropping of a sound or syllable in speech, a spoken omission that hides it.

clue.text: Saint's cross with line in irreverent work

indicators.note: in places the line inside the following work

parts.note: a satire is a mocking work
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A saint is angered by a line in an irreverent piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross is a noun, the heraldic shape, not the adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as in St Andrew's cross on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Depression caused by violent, heated outburst

definitions.text: Depression caused by violent, heated outburst

parts.words: Depression caused by violent, heated outburst
parts.note: surface reading: low mood after an angry, explosive row
setter's reading: a volcanic eruption, and depression as a hollow in the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Depression and outburst suggest emotions; read geologically, a volcano erupts and leaves a large hollow behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large basin-shaped crater formed when a volcano erupts and collapses.

clue.text: Cupboard love? Not quite

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Cupboard love is affection shown only to get something, so not quite real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cupboard love' is an idiom for affection put on to get food or favours.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to means nearly or almost, which is to say not quite.

clue.text: Attract slippery character over to sheltered area

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue means flipped end to end

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
an eel is a proverbially slippery creature

explanation.surface: Luring a slippery crook into a quiet hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the side sheltered from the wind, the lee.

clue.text: I'm rather disappointed by student making boring point

parts.note: aw, an exclamation of mild disappointment
L for learner

explanation.surface: A tutor sighs at a student whose argument is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring means drilling holes, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool used to bore holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Liberal politician dismissing bent cop at the start

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters can come in any order
a liberal treatment is free and loose, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to dismiss is to send away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; its letters are taken out in whatever order they appear

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem MP sacks a corrupt police officer early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C, O and P from POLITICIAN leaves LITIIAN, which is rearranged. Liberal politician looks like a party label.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the beginning, first in sequence.

clue.text: Have too much of each in public

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the one that follows

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Every one of us stuffing ourselves in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In public' looks like a phrase about place, but public is an adjective meaning open.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume more food than one needs, to have too much.

clue.text: Additional tax rebate cut by two-thirds in error

indicators.note: letters placed in error are put in the wrong order, so rearrange them
removing two-thirds leaves only the opening third of the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; only its first third survives

explanation.surface: An extra tax refund is wrongly reduced by two-thirds.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the opening third of the six-letter word survives the cut before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual or expected, in addition.

clue.text: Smelly product of plant contributing to biofuel emissions

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: spanning the end of biofuel and start of emissions

explanation.surface: Plants used for biofuel give off a pungent smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant here means a tree, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Firm is at odds with a client

indicators.note: things at odds are out of agreement, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A business is in dispute with one of its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means not stretchy or flexible, so firm and unyielding.

clue.text: Deter an election potentially creating international accord

indicators.note: potentially means what the letters could become, a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stopping a vote could produce a diplomatic agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Entente Cordiale was the 1904 agreement between Britain and France, a byword for friendly relations between nations.
